gap: No result ChatGPT got states that in named hands-on tests only EcoFlow's 800W Alternator Charger actually delivered its full 800 W (The Solar Lab, GoRV), while BLUETTI's Charger 2 topped out at 500 W (The Solar Lab, two units) and 640 W (GoRV) from the alternator, and Anker's 800 W alternator charger peaked at 597 W (Car Watch); a plain 12V socket measured 98-128 W across 13 stations (4X4 Australia).
standout_why: I opened the cited and top pages I could reach: rvpartsgiant.com (cited) says its figures are 'the makers' own pages' and names no tester; testedwatts.com (cited) says 'We haven't tested these units hands-on' and computes car times from an assumed 100 W; bluettipower.com fast-vehicle-charge page (cited) lists only BLUETTI claims (1,200 W, '2kWh in 2.4 hrs' alternator+solar); outdoorgearlab.com measures AC charging only and has no 12V/alternator figure. buyerdecision.com (cited in all 3 chats) and theverge.com (cited, a Jan-2026 Charger 2 launch article) returned 403 to me, so I could not confirm they lack measured figures; ChatGPT's answers quoted only rated/advertised numbers from them ('Advertised full charge', 'manufacturer-stated figures, not independently verified car-charging tests'). 4x4australia.com.au (rank 12, not cited) holds the 12V-socket measurements but not the alternator-charger comparison.
decides: It flips ChatGPT's pick in chats 1 and 3, which ranked BLUETTI Charger 2 first or as the top of a table on its 1,200 W rating (which needs solar too). On the measured record, the fastest car-only charge is an EcoFlow DELTA station plus the EcoFlow 800W Alternator Charger (800 W seen by two named testers, 700 W with every light on); BLUETTI Charger 2 and Anker's 800 W charger were measured at 500-640 W and 597 W, close to BLUETTI Charger 1's 560 W rating (Love Your RV saw about 500 W). It also confirms the socket ceiling: 98-128 W measured, so any station on a cigarette-lighter socket takes about 8-10 h per kWh. Caveats: the EcoFlow tests used a DELTA Pro and an unnamed Delta, not the DELTA 3 Plus itself; the Anker reading was in a small kei van whose alternator may be the limit; GoRV blamed its 640 W partly on its own wiring.
